subject: Request: trial top-up after handoff delay — BrightForge integration
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@brightforge.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: BrightForge: integration hold — trial timeline

Hi Stephanie / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We hit an unexpected blocker in our adapter handoff: the third-party webhook payload changed schema (missing customer_id in a small batch), which caused our ingestion job to fail and blocked our end-to-end demo. Our engineers are on it but estimate ~5 business days to validate and release the patch.

Given the delay, we risk missing the POC window with internal stakeholders. Can Redwood provide a short trial top-up (sandbox credits + 2-week extension) so the team can resume testing once the fix is in?

I can share logs and an excerpt of the failing payload — attaching a short integration_log_excerpt.txt. Procurement will also need an approval note for any timeline changes.

Elena
Elena Rossi
Integration Lead, BrightForge
elena@brightforge.com
+1 415 555 0199

Attachment: integration_log_excerpt.txt (text)
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena@brightforge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: BrightForge: integration hold — trial timeline

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and for sending the log.

We're sorry to hear about the webhook schema regression; that kind of third-party drift is unfortunately common. We can approve a temporary two-week trial extension and add 10k sandbox credits to the BrightForge pilot account to cover the re-run of tests, subject to a short follow-up:

- Can Marissa (our customer success) have the list of specific endpoints and an ETA for the patch?
- Please confirm Procurement contact for an approval note (Procurement email included below is fine).
- We'll attach a mutual action plan (MAP) that documents the new schedule and deliverables — see redline_mutual_action_plan.xlsx.

I'll put the extension approval on record here so Procurement has an email trail. If you confirm the ETA, we'll push the credits and extend the trial window from Dec 8 -> Dec 22.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Attachment: redline_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Dec 2025 08:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightForge: integration hold — webhook schema drift (tech note)

Forwarding Elena's log with a quick engineering read.

On Wed, 3 Dec 2025 at 09:12, Elena Rossi <elena@brightforge.com> wrote:
> Hi Stephanie / Marissa,
>
> Thanks again for the call this morning. We hit an unexpected blocker in our adapter handoff: the third-party webhook payload changed schema (missing customer_id in a small batch), which caused our ingestion job to fail and blocked our end-to-end demo. Our engineers are on it but estimate ~5 business days to validate and release the patch.

Engineering notes:
- The failure looks like a defensive assertion in their ingestion that required customer_id for mapping; we can add a permissive fallback in our adapter to accept nulls and surface a warning instead of failing the entire run.
- Quick mitigation: we can push a non-invasive config change to the sandbox adapter within 24 hours to accept the mutated payloads; full fix not required for the demo if they can tolerate warnings.
- Risk: permissive fallback could obscure downstream mapping issues; prefer coordinated fix but migration path exists.

If CS wants the quick config change, I can coordinate and schedule a 1-hour window with BrightForge engineers.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Rossi <elena@brightforge.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightforge.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Dec 2025 11:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: BrightForge: integration hold — trial timeline

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks — that approach sounds reasonable. Procurement is looped in (procurement@brightforge.com). We can target the quick config change first to keep the demo window, but the engineering team still wants the patch in our codebase (they expect the release by Tue, Dec 9).

Please treat this email as a request for the trial top-up + 2-week extension you mentioned; Procurement has asked for one formal approval email that they can attach to the SOW.

Also, can we lock a follow-up demo for Dec 15 (morning PST)? We want the internal PM and two stakeholder teams to attend — I'll send a calendar invite once the extension is confirmed.

Best,
Elena

Hi Elena / Procurement team —

This note confirms Redwood's approval for the following, tied to BrightForge pilot BF-2025-993:

1) Trial extension: add two calendar weeks to the current sandbox trial window. New expiry: 2025-12-22 (previous expiry 2025-12-08).
2) Sandbox credits: one-time top-up of 10,000 evaluation credits to the BrightForge test account.
3) Conditional clause: the extension and credits are granted to facilitate debugging and re-run of integration tests. We ask that BrightForge keep Redwood informed of the patch ETA; if the fix is not delivered by 2025-12-12, Redwood will engage with the CS team to reassess the timeline.

Next steps (action items):
- Elena: confirm the Dec 15 demo invite and attendee list.

- Marissa / Dylan: Marissa will schedule the config-change window (if BrightForge opts for the quick mitigation) and Dylan will coordinate deployment.
